cards.rule: "No" when nothing found in her record points toward ICE: 11 votes and 7 statements and actions point the other way.

items.t: Introduced a bill creating an office to provide mental health services to communities affected by immigration raids.
Made unannounced oversight visits to immigration detention facilities, including Adelanto (Oct 2026) and the Dilley family detention center in Texas (Jul 2026).
Voted Yea on H R 1689, To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status. It passed 224–204; Democrats 213–0.
Voted Nay on H R 1958, Deporting Fraudsters Act. It passed 231–186; Democrats 20–186.
Voted Nay on H R 7744, Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026. It passed 221–209; Democrats 4–209.
Called for ICE to be dismantled, saying it is “broken beyond repair” and a threat to public safety.
Issued three releases (Jan, Feb and Mar 2026) saying she voted “hell no” on funding bills for ICE and DHS.
Called for the impeachment of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.
Voted Nay on H R 3486, Stop Illegal Entry Act. It passed 226–197; Democrats 11–197.
Introduced an immigration bill after a constituent was transferred from the Adelanto detention center to Arizona.
Voted Nay on H RES 516, Condemning the violent June 2025 riots in Los Angeles, California. It passed 215–195; Democrats 7–195.
Voted Nay on H R 275, Special Interest Alien Reporting Act. It passed 231–182; Democrats 23–182.
Voted Nay on H R 2056, District of Columbia Federal Immigration Compliance Act. It passed 224–194; Democrats 11–194.
Voted Nay on H R 2931, Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act. It passed 211–199; Democrats 5–195.
Demanded answers and disciplinary action from ICE over what she called lawbreaking and misconduct during the Los Angeles raids.
Voted Nay on S 5, Laken Riley Act. It passed 263–156; Democrats 46–156.
Voted Nay on H R 30, Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act. It passed 274–145; Democrats 61–145.
Voted Nay on H R 29, Laken Riley Act. It passed 264–159; Democrats 48–159.

cards.rule: "Mixed" when at least 3 picked votes point each way. She cast 6 on the police or tough-on-crime side and 8 against.

items.t: Voted Yea on S 307, Prison Staff Safety Enhancement Act. It passed 376–8; Democrats 189–0.
Voted Yea on H R 5625, Cashless Bail Reporting Act. It passed 308–116; Democrats 96–114.
Voted Nay on H R 6260, Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act. It passed 243–179; Democrats 32–178.
Voted Yea on H RES 1252, Resolution memorializing law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty. It passed 418–2; Democrats 206–2.
Voted Nay on H CON RES 96, Expressing support for law enforcement officers. It passed 243–173; Democrats 29–173.
Voted Nay on H R 2853, Combating Organized Retail Crime Act. It passed 348–60; Democrats 144–59.
Voted Nay on H R 2189, Law-Enforcement Innovate to De-Escalate Act. It passed 233–185; Democrats 22–184.
Voted Nay on H R 5214, District of Columbia Cash Bail Reform Act. It passed 237–179; Democrats 28–179.
Voted Nay on H R 4922, DC CRIMES Act. It passed 240–179; Democrats 31–178.
Voted Yea on H R 747, Stop Chinese Fentanyl Act. It passed 407–4; Democrats 198–4.
Voted Nay on S 331, HALT Fentanyl Act. It passed 321–104; Democrats 104–103.
Voted Yea on H R 2240, Improving Law Enforcement Officer Safety and Wellness Through Data Act. It passed 403–11; Democrats 190–11.
Voted Yea on H CON RES 30, Expressing support for local law enforcement officers. It passed 411–1; Democrats 197–1.
Voted Nay on H R 27, HALT Fentanyl Act. It passed 312–108; Democrats 98–107.

cards.rule: Her votes decide the headline: all 16 business, finance and labor votes picked went the consumer or labor way. It is "Mostly no" rather than "No" because corporate PAC money to her campaign roughly tripled.

items.t: Voted Nay on the Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act. It passed 295–128; Democrats 83–128.
Introduced a bill to hold oil and gas companies accountable for pollution.
Voted Nay on the Main Street Act. It passed 270–155; Democrats 56–154.
Voted Yea on the Faster Labor Contracts Act. It passed 230–193; Democrats 210–0.
Voted Nay on the fuel-retailer (E15) bill, which Jeffries voted for. It passed 218–203; Democrats 95–113.
Took $124,790 from 53 corporate PACs in 2025–26, up from $42,500 from 19 in 2023–24, including defense contractors and drug companies.
Took $99,000 from trade associations and cooperatives in 2025–26, up from $51,834 in 2023–24.
Labor PACs gave $144,500 in 2025–26, compared with $124,790 from corporate PACs.
Voted Nay on the Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act. It passed 223–190; Democrats 15–190.
Voted Nay on the DUMP Red Tape Act. It passed 269–146; Democrats 59–146.
Voted Nay on the Electric Supply Chain Act. It passed 267–159; Democrats 51–159.
Voted Nay on the Increasing Investor Opportunities Act. It passed 302–123; Democrats 87–123.
Voted Nay on the Mining Regulatory Clarity Act. It passed 219–198; Democrats 9–197.
Voted Yea on the Protect America's Workforce Act, restoring federal workers' collective bargaining. It passed 231–195; Democrats 211–0.
Her Streamlining American Manufacturing Strategy Act, pitched as removing “manufacturing hurdles” for industry, became law as Section 8802 of the FY2026 defense bill (which she voted against).
Voted Nay on the CLARITY Act, the crypto industry's market-structure bill. It passed 294–134; Democrats 78–134.
Voted Nay on the GENIUS Act on stablecoins, which Jeffries voted for. It passed 308–122; Democrats 102–110.
Voted Nay on repealing the consumer bureau's rule on big-tech payment apps (S.J. Res. 28). It passed 219–211; Democrats 0–211.
Voted Nay on repealing the consumer bureau's overdraft-fee rule (S.J. Res. 18). It passed 217–211; Democrats 0–210.
Voted Nay on the repeal of the IRS rule requiring crypto platforms to report user transactions (H.J. Res. 25). It passed 292–132; Democrats 76–132.
Voted Nay on the Midnight Rules Relief Act, letting Congress repeal batches of late-term regulations. It passed 212–208; Democrats 1–207.
